flags.why: The common physical sense of crossing or cutting across something is missing.
flags.fix: Add: to cross; to cut across, as in 'Con đường cắt ngang cánh đồng.' = 'The road cuts across the field.'

flags.why: The phrase means assigning turns or shifts, rather than taking turns or working shifts ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-c%E1%BA%AFt)).
flags.fix: to assign turns; to allocate shifts

flags.why: This expression is used throughout Vietnam, including in Southern speech ([usage example](https://www.webtretho.vn/f/toc-nail/cac-me-oi-cho-em-hoi-o-sai-gon-cat-toc-tem-o-dau-dep-vay-a-1869383)).
Cutting someone's hair is expressed with cắt tóc throughout Vietnam ([Southern usage](https://classic.vn/danh-sach-nhung-tiem-toc-barber-shop-cuc-chat-tai-sai-gon/)).
The expression for the act or service of cutting hair is nationwide ([Southern usage](https://lamtocdepgovap.com/cat-toc/cat-toc-dep-go-vap-hair-salon-cat-toc-dep-chuyen-nghiep-sai-gon.html)).
This political pun is commonly used to mock communists and needs a derogatory warning.
The example explains the spelling substitution instead of using the political meaning.
flags.fix: Nó lại chửi cọng sả trên mạng. = He is insulting communists online again.

flags.why: This sense belongs to literary or elevated language rather than ordinary casual descriptions of someone's character.
